intro: The decision cannot be closed on published data alone. Each question states what is already answered from official sources, what is missing, and exactly who to ask. 'Blocks' refers to the six-step decision sequence on the Summary page.

items.question: What are the exact trip dates and how many nights?
items.what_we_have: The only dated, published schedule in scope is The Venetian's DeepStack Extravaganza IV, November 16 - December 23, 2026 (94 published rows). Any date outside that window has no verified tournament anchor at all.
items.what_is_missing: Your arrival and departure dates. Every rate, availability and cancellation answer depends on them.
items.how_to_find: You decide. Once fixed, the booking deep links on the Hotels page and the rate log carry them, and the checker compares your checkout total against the modelled cost.
items.blocks: everything downstream: hotel quote, walking test, room-rate eligibility

items.question: What is the nightly budget ceiling and the quality floor?
items.what_we_have: One official rate statement exists: Venetian/Palazzo poker suite rates 'start as low as $119 and $209', with a $55 resort fee and a 13.38% county room tax. Park MGM publishes a $50 resort fee plus tax and $20/day guest parking. That is enough to build two cost bands, not to pick a winner.
items.what_is_missing: Your ceiling per night and your minimum acceptable quality tier; no hotel publishes a rating on its own pages (FG-12).
items.how_to_find: Answer here, then choose a rating source (suggestion S-04) so quality becomes a comparable field instead of an adjective.

items.question: Is the event you want actually single-entry?
items.what_we_have: Ten structure sheets read in full: none of the one-day sheets contains a rebuy, add-on or re-entry clause. The Valuetown sheet proves the room writes such clauses when they exist (rule 07: 'All subsequent buy in's after the initial buy in will be $200'), so the 34 one-day rows without such language are treated as candidates, not confirmations.
items.what_is_missing: A one-line written answer from the poker room for the specific events you enter.
items.how_to_find: Venetian poker room: 702.414.7657 or lv_cas_poker@venetianlasvegas.com (both printed on the official poker page). Ask: 'is Event NN limited to one entry, with no rebuy or add-on?' and keep the reply.
items.blocks: whether any event qualifies at all (FG-02)

items.question: What is the total cost to enter - is the advertised number fee-inclusive?
items.what_we_have: For all 94 Venetian rows (all 37 sheets read as of 2026-11-17), yes and it is stated per event: e.g. '$58 of the $300 Buy-In is withheld for house fees (Rake - Staff). The prize pool consists of $242 of every $300 Buy In.' So the buy-in is the total you pay; the fee is carved out of it, not added.
items.what_is_missing: Nothing for the Venetian DSE IV events. The remaining special cases are the PokerAtlas Valuetown events, where a PRO member pays $180 instead of $200 for the first entry, and the early-registration rake discounts (Events 56 and 59) which are noted on their rows.
items.how_to_find: Excerpts are on each row; ask the cage only if you want the rule re-confirmed verbally.
items.blocks: ranking, because the guarantee-to-cost ratio changes if the fee is additive

items.question: What does the guarantee actually contain?
items.what_we_have: Bounty events state it: 'A Prize Pool of $8,000 is guaranteed by the Venetian Poker Room which consists of the actual prize pool plus the total amount of $50 bounties that are awarded.' So the headline guarantee is cash-plus-bounties, not cash to the field.
items.what_is_missing: Nothing for the Venetian sheets - all 37 are read as of 2026-11-17; each row's guarantee excerpt states whether bounties are included. The satellites guarantee seats, not dollars (2 direct entries into Events #39/#47).
items.how_to_find: Already in the sheet excerpt on each row.
items.blocks: comparing a $300 bounty event against a $300 flat event

items.question: How deep do payouts run, and does that change the ratio's meaning?
items.what_we_have: 'This event pays 12.5% of the field' on every one-day sheet read. Combined with the guarantee that gives a per-cash-place floor you can compute; the site shows guarantee divided by buy-in as a descriptive size ratio only.
items.what_is_missing: Field size, which nobody can know before the event. Any 'expected value' claim would be invented.
items.how_to_find: Only the day's registration count; the results column on the official page stays empty until the event runs.
items.blocks: turning the ratio into a ranking criterion - it must stay descriptive

items.question: Which events can realistically be stacked in one day?
items.what_we_have: Registration windows and level lengths from the sheets: the 11:10 AM events close late registration at ~4:55 PM, the 5:10 PM events at 9:40 PM, the 10:10 AM RaceDay events at 12:25 PM. So the RaceDay format is the only one that can plausibly finish before an 11:10 AM event; the 5:10 PM event is a late-entry fallback, never a clean second full field.
items.what_is_missing: Actual finish times. No official source publishes average or expected duration, so 'earliest plausible finish' is a derived clock value, labelled as such on the Schedule page.
items.how_to_find: Two live days of observation, or the room's own estimate when you call for Q-03.
items.blocks: the 'one event per day, evening only if you can exit' rule

items.question: What is the true nightly cost for your stay - itemised?
items.what_we_have: Every component except the room rate: $55 fee plus tax, 13.38% room tax, $50/night per additional guest 13+ (Venetian), $40/night per additional occupant (Park MGM), $20/day guest parking, $150/night (Venetian) or $100/day (Park MGM) incidentals, $100 plus tax for checking out early at the Venetian, Wynn bundling free self-parking for two vehicles into its fee and charging a $50 extra-guest surcharge.
items.what_is_missing: A dated, per-night room rate for your dates, from the booking page or the itemised checkout total. Nothing else is missing from the formula.
items.how_to_find: Open the official booking deep link on the Hotels page, select your room and copy the itemisation into the rate log format (the log template is on the Rate Log page).

items.question: Which cancellation deadline applies to your booking?
items.what_we_have: Park MGM: first night's deposit refundable if cancelled at least 72 hours before arrival. Wynn: full-stay deposit taken at booking; two official offer pages show 48-hour and 72-hour windows. Venetian: deposit at booking (first night or whole stay); prepaid offers are non-cancellable and non-refundable, with no general hour stated.
items.what_is_missing: The deadline attached to the specific rate you book - it is offer-coded, not property-wide.
items.how_to_find: It is printed on the reservation confirmation and in the checkout terms; compare it against the tournament start you have committed to.
items.blocks: the sequencing rule: confirm schedules before non-refundable payment (step 6)

items.question: Is the walk actually under 30 minutes - and does it stay outdoors?
items.what_we_have: Two official route facts: the poker room is inside the Palazzo (in-resort directions published, no minutes) and Bellagio/Cosmopolitan/Vdara share an interior bridge. The Venetian complex is the tournament anchor for every row in the ranked table.
items.what_is_missing: A minute value for every hotel-to-room pair, including the crossing at Las Vegas Blvd and Tropicana, plus whether the route is covered (a real factor in August, not in December).
items.how_to_find: Use the Google/Apple Maps links on the Walking page for each pair, or approve S-06 so the daily job records durations from a routing API.
items.blocks: the 30-minute filter, which today correctly returns 'unknown' for every pair (FG-11)

items.question: Do the hotel's poker-rate conditions survive your schedule?
items.what_we_have: The Venetian poker rate requires, per night, either six hours of active live cash play or a $300-or-higher tournament buy-in, completed before 2 AM on the last night. The $200 RaceDay Stack and the $200 Bounty events do not qualify a night on their own, even though they are the cheapest entries in the series.
items.what_is_missing: Whether six cash-game hours is realistic between 11:10 AM and 4:55 PM registration - it is not, so the plan must include a $300+ entry every night or accept the prevailing rate.
items.how_to_find: Your own schedule: the plan builder already prefers $300+ events for exactly this reason.
items.blocks: the difference between a $119 and a prevailing-rate night, which can double the lodging cost

items.question: Are the schedules still standing the week before you fly?
items.what_we_have: An official disclaimer on every structure sheet: 'Management reserves the right to cancel or change the tournament.' The change monitor now re-reads every official URL daily and reports value-level differences.
items.what_is_missing: A pre-payment re-check ritual: series page, event sheet, hotel rate, cancellation deadline, all on the same day.
items.how_to_find: The Change report page shows the last run and which sources moved; re-run the workflow manually (workflow_dispatch) the morning you pay.

items.question: Which Strip rooms have been left out, and does that change the answer?
items.what_we_have: Only The Venetian's schedule is in the ranked dataset, because it is the only one with a dated, per-event official document set we have read. Wynn, Caesars Palace, Horseshoe, MGM Grand, Bellagio, ARIA and Golden Nugget appear in the spend-advantage / unverified tables with their official links.
items.what_is_missing: Bellagio's three weekly term sheets, MGM's dated schedule, ARIA's current calendar, plus Planet Hollywood, LINQ, Paris, Luxor/Excalibur/NY-NY and downtown (Circa, The STRAT) - none read in this pass.
items.how_to_find: Suggestion S-03: read one venue per refresh run and grow the same three-state classification, instead of trusting an aggregator.
items.blocks: the claim that these Venetian events are the 'best' on the Strip - today it is only 'the best verified'

items.question: Who is coming, and does sharing change the cost?
items.what_we_have: Occupancy economics: the Venetian's rate is quoted on single/double occupancy and adds $50/night per guest aged 13+; Park MGM adds $40 plus tax per occupant above two; Wynn adds $50 per night above the room's stated capacity and caps standard rooms at four people ($500 per person beyond the cap, up to $3,000).
items.what_is_missing: Party size. Two players splitting a $119+fee room halves the lodging cost per player and doubles the qualifying-play obligation, since play from all registered guests counts toward the requirement.
items.how_to_find: Decide the party; the trip calculator has an occupancy control that applies the surcharge lines automatically.
items.blocks: the per-player cost comparison between hotels
